purpose: Rank mapped candidate areas by the strongest defensible method supported by the uploaded observations, topology and travel-time history.

execution_tiers.name: Observed fixed-grid degradation
required_data: one measured metric with confirmed severity semantics
execution_tiers.claim: Descriptive geographic cells ranked by mean observed relative degradation

execution_tiers.name: Regional Dynamic Propagation Connectivity
required_data: at least two valid travel-time observations per retained link
at least two 5 km cells with 10 valid routable links each
execution_tiers.accepted_input: For each row, positive uploaded travel time is used first; otherwise travel time is deterministically derived from positive speed and positive link length
execution_tiers.claim: Regional propagation sensitivity under one uploaded historical network state

mathematical_formulation.travel_time_reference: T^0_ij = Q_0.05({T_ij(tau)}) using the platform's disclosed lower empirical quantile rule
mathematical_formulation.platform_dpc: Finite deterministic trapezoidal approximation to Equation (9), using the returned scaled horizon, sample count and numerical basis dimension
mathematical_formulation.regional_degradation: a_ij^(-R,alpha) = (1-alpha) a_ij for links in candidate region R, with alpha=0.5

numerical_contract.quadrature: 33 propagation-time samples over a dimensionless scaled horizon of 30
numerical_contract.hardware: Classical CPU numerical linear algebra. No quantum-computing claim is made.

primary_sources.citation: Xu, J., Niu, C., Dixit, V., Nair, D.J. and Zhang, T. (2026). Quantum percolation based dynamic propagation connectivity for critical-area identification in transport networks. arXiv:2606.30242v1.
primary_sources.relationship: Equations (3) to (20) define the travel-time propagation operator, DPC and regional perturbation score implemented by the high-data tier. The preprint settings q=0.05, alpha=0.5, 5 km cells and minimum support 10 are retained.
primary_sources.evidence_status: Preprint submitted 29 June 2026. The platform identifies this status and does not describe the method as peer reviewed.

primary_sources.citation: Jenelius, E. and Mattsson, L.-G. (2012). Road network vulnerability analysis of area-covering disruptions: A grid-based approach with case study. Transportation Research Part A, 46(5), 746-760.
primary_sources.relationship: Supports the reproducible candidate-region partition and the distinction between area analysis and individual-link ranking.

primary_sources.citation: Mülken, O. and Blumen, A. (2011). Continuous-time quantum walks: Models for coherent transport on complex networks. Physics Reports, 502(2-3), 37-87.
Guo, K. and Mohar, B. (2017). Hermitian adjacency matrix of digraphs and mixed graphs. Journal of Graph Theory, 85(1), 217-248.
primary_sources.relationship: Supports Hermitian representations for directed and mixed graphs.

verification_contract: Every scored link belongs to the uploaded project and one deterministic 5 km cell
No invalid or non-positive travel time enters the propagation operator
At least 80% of eligible routable mapped links support the DPC tier
Every DPC candidate cell contains at least 10 valid routable links
The operator is Hermitian within floating-point tolerance
Every regional score is finite and non-negative
Repeated inputs return identical ranks and diagnostics
known_limitations: The arXiv paper defines an infinite propagation-time average but does not publish a finite quadrature configuration. The platform therefore reports its own reproducible finite numerical contract.

The paper replaces rare invalid observations with the nearest valid same-link observation. This platform does not impute across times; it requires at least 80% valid current-and-history link coverage and reports the retained coverage.
The paper defines regular grids over each study network. The platform uses a globally anchored EPSG:3857 5 km grid so cell identity remains stable across viewports and repeated runs.

Speed/length-derived travel time is a dimensionally consistent platform fallback, but it need not reproduce observed link travel time; the paper's empirical application uses observed link travel time.
The Lanczos residual is a visible projection-boundary diagnostic, not a certified error bound for infinite-time DPC.
The platform run evaluates the chosen historical observation time. A full time-averaged paper replication requires every retained time and is outside the interactive run.
The 5 km cells are screening units. They are not hazard footprints, administrative areas or causal impact zones.
DPC measures propagation sensitivity. Population exposure, equity, demand-weighted delay and hazard probability require separate data and models.
